cues.text: Every number in the next two chapters rests on one assumption about how revenue moves. So we build that first, and we build it with coins.
Each year, revenue does one of two things. It goes up by a fixed percentage, or down by one.
Percentages rather than pounds, because a big firm swings by big amounts and a small one by small amounts. That is the only realistic way to do it.
Do that again the next year, and the next. Every point splits in two, and the possibilities fan out.
Watch one possible path through it. That is one future — one thing that might happen.
And here are a dozen more. Nobody knows which one happens. All anybody knows is the shape of the fan.
a random walk. Each step is up or down by a fixed percentage, and you cannot tell which.
Take a typical year and ask: how far did revenue move? In a calm trade, not far. The outcomes bunch up.
In a rough trade — oil, metals — they spread right out.

The width of that spread is the number the paper calls the choppiness. It is the size of a typical yearly swing, written as a percentage. Ten per cent for revenue that moves with exchange rates. Twenty-five to forty for an oil well or a copper mine. And the paper's base case sits between, at twenty.
The paper writes it as a Greek letter. This film never will. It is the choppiness, and it is a percentage.
